body.statement: For the finite family of vector subspaces \(\{W_j(C):j\in L\}\), there are representatives \(w_j\in W_j(C)\) that are linearly independent if and only if \(\dim(\sum_{j\in J}W_j(C))\geq |J|\) for every \(J\subseteq L\).

source.locator: Theorem 1, specialized to the vector matroid
source.verbatim_statement: Let W₁, W₂, ..., Wᵣ be subspaces of an ambient vector space V. Then a system of linearly independent representatives of the Wᵢ exists if and only if for each subset I ⊆ [r], dim(∑ᵢ∈I Wᵢ) ⩾ |I|.

upstream.citation: R. Rado, A theorem on independence relations, Quarterly Journal of Mathematics os-13(1):83–89, 1942, DOI 10.1093/qmath/os-13.1.83.
upstream.locator: Theorem 1; exact vector-space restatement in Le 2021, Theorem 3.1

attestation.note: Verified in the lawful open-access Numdam PDF of Ian Le, Intersection Pairings for Higher Laminations, Algebraic Combinatorics 4(5), 2021, Theorem 3.1 (Rado), which explicitly identifies this as the specialization of Rado’s matroid theorem; the original OUP record is paywalled.
